items.headline: Parliament committee wants €200bn for the next Horizon Europe
items.body: The European Parliament's industry and research committee (ITRE) adopted its position on Horizon Europe 2028–2034 on 10 November by 67 votes to 1, with 18 abstentions. MEPs ask for an overall budget of €200 billion in current prices, against the €175 billion the Commission proposed. Parliament also wants new 'Horizon Europe Pathway actions' to take research results into deployment, commercialisation and scale-up.
items.what_it_means: This is Parliament's opening position before talks with the Council, not the final budget. For research-driven clients, the signal is that the next programme is likely to be larger and more focused on getting results to market — worth building exploitation and scale-up plans into 2027 proposals now.

items.headline: MEPs back a €264bn European Competitiveness Fund and €91bn for CEF
items.body: On the same day, ITRE adopted its position on the European Competitiveness Fund (ECF) by 61 votes to 13, with 12 abstentions. From 2028 to 2034 the Fund would pool 14 existing EU funding instruments, and the committee also wants a dedicated defence research programme. Separately, ITRE and TRAN asked for €91.28 billion for the Connecting Europe Facility 2028–2034. Both mandates still need approval in the 23–26 November plenary.
items.what_it_means: The 2028–2034 funding map is taking shape: many programmes clients use today (including parts of Digital Europe and the EIC) would sit inside the ECF. Nothing changes for current calls, but long-term funding roadmaps should now plan for the ECF structure.

items.headline: EIC 2027 Work Programme adopted: €1.8bn, the last under Horizon Europe
items.body: The Commission adopted the European Innovation Council's 2027 Work Programme, making €1.8 billion available for deep-tech researchers and companies. It is the final EIC package under Horizon Europe 2021–2027 and completes the €1 billion Scaleup Europe Fund, with €200 million for defence investments and €25 million for the Advanced Innovation Challenges pilot. EIC Accelerator cut-offs in 2027 are 20 January, 17 March, 1 September and 4 November; the first EIC Pathfinder deadline is 25 February 2027.
items.what_it_means: Only four Accelerator cut-offs next year, so timing matters more: teams aiming for 20 January need their short application through now. The EIC online info day on 19 November is the place to check the scheme changes.

items.headline: EU launches €525M European Chip Design Platform
items.body: The Commission launched the European Chip Design Platform (EuroCDP) under the Chips Act. It mobilises €525 million: €440 million in grants of up to €16 million for chip design companies, and €85 million for the platform's infrastructure, support services and open-source design tools. €285 million comes from the EU budget and €240 million from Chips Joint Undertaking participating states. Grant applications are open on the platform's website.
items.what_it_means: A direct, non-dilutive route for semiconductor start-ups and SMEs, alongside access to design tools, IP blocks and manufacturing capacity. Hardware clients should check eligibility now while the first grant rounds are open.

items.headline: AI Act: grace period for AI-content marking ends 2 December
items.body: Under the Digital Omnibus on AI, generative AI systems already on the market before 2 August 2026 have until 2 December 2026 to meet the Article 50(2) duty to mark synthetic output in a machine-readable format. Systems placed on the market from 2 August 2026 get no grace period, and the other Article 50 transparency duties, such as chatbot disclosure and deepfake labelling, already apply.
items.what_it_means: Clients with generative AI products on the market before August have about two weeks left to build marking in. Newer products need it from launch, and it is worth confirming the exact wording against the Official Journal text.

items.headline: redalpine closes $250M early-stage science fund
items.body: Zurich-founded pan-European VC redalpine closed its early-stage fund redalpine capital VIII at $250 million on 10 November 2026.
items.what_it_means: Early-stage capital for science-based companies is still being raised. For EU grant holders, a strong Horizon or EIC result is a useful signal to bring into conversations with funds like these.

items.headline: Commission proposes the European Innovation Act
items.body: The European Commission published its proposal for a European Innovation Act on 9 September 2026, as a regulation that would apply directly in all Member States. It sets a common EU framework for valuing intellectual property, a digital marketplace for IP assets and a common procedure for public R&D procurement, alongside a separate proposal on regulatory sandboxes. The Commission estimates the IP-financing measures could unlock up to €10.2bn a year in IP-backed venture capital and debt. It is a proposal only: it now goes to the European Parliament and the Council, and it creates no new funding programme.
items.what_it_means: Nothing changes for applicants yet, but it is worth tracking for clients whose main asset is IP: a common valuation method would make IP-backed financing easier, and joint cross-border R&D procurement could become a new route to market for deep-tech suppliers to public buyers.

items.headline: Scaleup Europe Fund makes its first investment in ICEYE
items.body: The €5bn-target Scaleup Europe Fund, managed by EQT, announced its first investment on 5 August 2026 by co-leading ICEYE's €1bn Series F round, which includes €450m of primary investment at a valuation above €10bn. The fund invests directly in European deep-tech companies from Series B onwards, with the Commission contributing €1bn from the EIC part of Horizon Europe alongside private investors.
items.what_it_means: The fund is now deploying capital, which sets the bar for what it backs: large, late-stage rounds in strategic sectors such as space. For earlier-stage deep-tech clients it is a signal for the scale-up path after EIC Accelerator, not a source for the next round.

items.headline: Digital Omnibus on AI enters into force
items.body: The Digital Omnibus on AI — Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 — was published in the Official Journal on 24 July and entered into force on 27 July, three days ahead of the standard timeline so it could take effect before the 2 August deadline it amends. Article 50 transparency obligations (AI-system disclosure, deepfake labelling, disclosure of AI-generated content published on matters of public interest) still apply from 2 August 2026. The compliance deadline for stand-alone high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III is now 2 December 2027, and for high-risk AI embedded in regulated products (Annex I) it is 2 August 2028.
items.what_it_means: Deep-tech clients building Annex III high-risk systems — employment, education, critical infrastructure — get genuine breathing room on compliance, and those embedding high-risk AI in regulated products now have until August 2028; but the 2 August transparency duties still apply regardless of either extension, so it's worth flagging all three clocks separately. Also a timely compliance-relief note for any client who was scrambling ahead of the original 2 August deadline.
